name: flow-agent
description: Agents in terminals (Claude Code, Codex or any agent CLI) with the Agents dock, using each repo's own harness; the chat panel over ACP behind a setting.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Agents run commands in your workspace, so none can be started until you trust this folder.

chatSessions.name: claude
chatSessions.description: Claude Code with this repo's CLAUDE.md, hooks and skills
chatSessions.welcomeMessage: Runs your local Claude Code with this repo's harness: CLAUDE.md, hooks, skills, MCP.

chatSessions.name: codex
chatSessions.description: OpenAI Codex CLI with this repo's AGENTS.md
chatSessions.welcomeMessage: Runs your local Codex CLI with this repo's AGENTS.md. Sign in once with `codex login`.

colors.description: Manual mode: asks before every change.

commands.title: New Claude Agent in a Worktree
New Codex Agent in a Worktree

flow.agents.showChat.description: Also offer Claude and Codex in the chat panel. Off by default: agents run in terminals and the Agents dock shows their status.

flow.agents.custom.description: Your own agent commands, offered in Start an Agent. User settings only: a repository's .vscode/settings.json cannot add commands that run in your terminal.

command.description: Run in a new terminal in the workspace folder.

acceptsInput.description: Questions from Home and "Ask about this flow" may be typed into its prompt. Off by default: Axle cannot see whether a custom agent is waiting at its prompt or at an approval question.

flow.agents.askTarget.markdownDescription: Where questions for the agent go (Home's prompt, **Ask about this flow**): `remember` (default) asks once per workspace and then uses that choice (change it with **Axle: Change Agent for Questions…** or the note in the status bar after sending); `ask` asks every time; `claude`, `codex` or `custom:<name>` always use that CLI (a session waiting at its prompt, else a new one); `chat` the chat panel; `clipboard` copies the question.

flow.agents.mcp.markdownDescription: Give agents started from Axle the `axle` tools (open files, the git diff and flows in the editor, find entry points, symbols, definitions and references, read diagnostics and flows as text, draw diagrams and plans). They are added to the agent with `--mcp-config`, next to your own MCP servers; they cannot write files or run commands. Takes effect for agents started afterwards.

flow.agents.shim.markdownDescription: Also give a `claude` you type by hand in an Axle terminal the `axle` tools (open the diff, show flows, find symbols, diagnostics). Axle puts a small `claude` script first on the PATH of its own terminals; it runs the real `claude` with `--mcp-config` added, and passes subcommands such as `claude mcp` through untouched. Requires `#flow.agents.mcp#`. Takes effect after reloading the window.

flow.agents.gaze.description: Show where agents started in Axle are reading and editing on a flow canvas that is open: a dot on the card they read and a fading trail of the cards they visited. Only files and lines are passed on, never file content or search text, and only in memory. Turn off to send nothing.

axle.skeletonFirst.enabled.description: Skeleton first: after you approve a plan that adds or changes types, entities or interfaces, the agent draws its design and you write the skeleton (types, signatures, empty bodies) yourself; the board shows your code against the design, the agent checks and explains, then fills the bodies. Offered, never imposed: "Just do it" is always one click. Also the switch at the top of the Agents dock.

flow.agents.planBoard.description: When an agent proposes a plan (leaves plan mode), draw it as a board in Axle and tick its steps as the agent edits the files they point at.

flow.agents.turnImpact.description: When an agent finishes a turn, show on its row which flows (endpoints) the files it edited may affect.

flow.agents.notify.approval.description: Notify when an agent waits for your approval (a permission or a plan) while you look elsewhere: another window, or another terminal.

flow.agents.notify.question.description: Notify when an agent asks you a question while you look elsewhere.

flow.agents.notify.error.description: Notify when an agent hits an error (an API error, a run of failing tool calls, a crash) while you look elsewhere.

flow.agents.notify.done.description: Notify when an agent finishes a turn while you look elsewhere.

flow.agents.notify.quiet.description: Quiet mode: no agent notifications at all. The Agents dock still ranks and marks what needs you.

enumDescriptions: Gyro: rings that tumble while the agent works, one ring that pulses while it waits for you; the dot on the outer arc is the agent (its colour) and the arc is how full its context window is
Pixel pets: a cat (Claude), a bunny (Codex) and a bear (other agents) whose faces show what they do
flow.agents.avatar.description: How agents are drawn in the Agents dock and in the desktop status overlay.

flow.agents.desktop.badge.markdownDescription: Show how many agents need you (the Agents dock badge: approvals, questions, errors and finished turns you have not looked at) on the app icon: the Dock on macOS, an overlay on the taskbar button on Windows, the launcher on Linux. Desktop app only. `#flow.agents.notify.quiet#` does not hide it: a count is not an interruption.

flow.agents.desktop.overlay.enabled.markdownDescription: A small status overlay that stays on top of other apps and shows each live agent with its state: working, needs you (approval, question, error) or done. It never takes focus; clicking an agent shows its terminal in Axle. On a Mac with a notch, `top-center` sits over the notch. Desktop app only. Independent of `#flow.agents.desktop.badge#`.

enumDescriptions: Top middle of the screen: over the notch on a Mac that has one, a pill elsewhere
flow.agents.desktop.overlay.position.description: Where the status overlay sits on its screen.

enumDescriptions: The screen the Axle window is on (it follows the window)
The first screen that is not the primary one (the primary one when there is only one)
flow.agents.desktop.overlay.display.description: Which screen the status overlay is on.

enumDescriptions: A pill with a dot per agent and the counts; hover lists the agents
Only a dot per agent; hover lists the agents
Always the list: name, state and activity of each agent
flow.agents.desktop.overlay.style.description: How the status overlay draws the agents.

flow.agents.desktop.overlay.size.description: How large the status overlay is.

flow.agents.desktop.overlay.opacity.description: How opaque the status overlay is, from 0.3 to 1.

enumDescriptions: Pure black with hairline edges: the island look
The colours of Axle's colour theme
flow.agents.desktop.overlay.theme.description: The colours of the status overlay.

needsYou.description: Agents that need you: an approval, a question or an error

done.description: Agents that finished a turn you have not looked at

idle.description: Idle and starting agents, and finished turns you have read

counts.description: How many need you, work and are done

activity.description: What each agent does, as a verb (Running, Editing) unless details are on

context.description: How full each agent's context window is, as a small ring

cost.description: Each session's cost in dollars, where the CLI reports it

elapsed.description: How long each agent has been in its state

noAgents.description: Hide when no agent is shown

axleFocused.description: Hide while an Axle window has focus

flow.agents.desktop.overlay.autoHide.description: When the status overlay hides itself.

flow.agents.desktop.overlay.details.description: Show the command, file name or question in the status overlay's activity line, not only a verb. The overlay is on top of every app, so leave this off when you share your screen.

flow.agents.worktree.markdownDescription: Start each new Claude Code and Codex agent in a git worktree of its own: a checkout under `.axle/worktrees/<name>` on a new branch `axle/<name>`, cut from the branch you are on. Agents working in parallel then never write over each other's files; the agent's row shows the branch, how far it is ahead of and behind its base, and buttons to open it, show its changes in flow, merge it back and remove it. Axle git-ignores `.axle/` in the repository's `.git/info/exclude`. Off: agents work in this checkout ("Other…" in the Agents dock still offers a worktree).

flow.agents.codexHooks.description: Show Codex's status (working, needs you, done) and its edits on the canvas. Axle writes read-only hooks to its own Codex profile ($CODEX_HOME/axle.config.toml) and starts Codex with `-p axle`; your config.toml is not changed. Codex asks you once to trust these hooks (/hooks).
